review_basis: Hand-traced in the running canvas app's Linear tool (manual mode, scale confirmed from the plan's own '1/4" = 1'-0"' note) via a Playwright-driven browser session against the rendered PDF, following the run centerlines visually and reading segment sizes directly off the drawn duct-size text before committing each segment. The THIRD run ('bessemer-m101-bed2-transfer-stub') was added later, under GATE 3's own single-call trace-engine testing: this sheet's two horizontal trunks above are both entirely wall-vouch-excluded from `trace_run` (docs/LINEAR-TRACE-EVAL.md's own Finding 1 -- long, straight, axis-dominant runs with no layer signal on this unlayered sheet), so a grid-sweep for a DIFFERENT, single-call-friendly real run on this same sheet was run instead. It found this file's own already-disclosed '14x3½ stub serving Bedroom 2' (named in this file's own original `scope` field as real, identified linework that was simply out of scope for GATE 1's 'supply mains' purpose) -- confirmed independently via a marked render crop (both ends real: a T-off from the vertical 8"ø riser on one side, a stop just short of the TG-1 transfer-grille's own transition boot on the other) and via `mcp/scripts/graph-render.mjs`'s DIFFUSER, GRILLE, REGISTER SCHEDULE render, which gives TG-1's own NECK SIZE as '14 x 6' -- confirming '14x3½' is NOT the register's neck size and is therefore the duct run's own size, not a mislabeled schedule value. `trace_run`'s own automatic label-bind came back blank here (`size_missing`, `stroke-family:unclassified` -- the same unlayered-sheet, no-family-evidence path as the sheet's other runs); the size is a direct read off the sheet's own drawn callout, the same precedent `ground_truth/linear/baker-m101-heldout.json` already established for a label sitting just outside `trace_run`'s own binding radius. `system: "TA"` (transfer air) is this annotator's own descriptive label, not one of this corpus's usual SA/RA/EA/OA/MA tokens -- TG-1 is a SCHEDULED TRANSFER GRILLE (moves air between two interior spaces, not to/from a supply or exhaust main), a real category this corpus's existing vocabulary has no clean slot for; `run.system` is documentation only here (not read by any bench scoring code -- checked directly in bench/linear.mts/score.ts before relying on that), so this costs nothing to leave honestly labeled rather than forced into a wrong SA/RA/EA guess. scope: GATE 1 asks for Bessemer M101's supply mains. This sheet draws two independent horizontal supply-duct trunks, one per first-floor heat-pump unit (HP-1), each running from its heat pump's boot connection out to its farthest labeled diffuser/register, with an explicit rectangular-duct size change partway along. Both are in scope as the sheet's 'supply mains' (plural, matching GATE 1's own wording). Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the first two runs: the round vertical branch/riser drops off each trunk (6"ø and 8"ø stubs down to the SR-1/SR-2 registers), and the 4" EA exhaust duct riser (near keynote 2, EF-1). The THIRD run brings in the short 14x3½ stub serving Bedroom 2 (a branch off the vertical 8"ø riser to the TG-1 transfer grille) that the original GATE 1 pass named but deliberately left out as not a horizontal main -- now included for a different, later purpose (GATE 3 single-call trace-engine recall testing), where its short, dead-end-bounded shape is exactly what a fair single-`trace_run`-call comparison needs, unlike the two heavily-branched trunks above (see review_basis). General note 1 on the sheet ('UNIT 103 MECHANICAL LAYOUT IS TYPICAL OF ALL UNITS EXCEPT UNIT 102') is why Units 101/104 show no drawn ductwork on this sheet -- there is nothing there to trace.
